findings.summary: 判据 2a's discriminating test still does not drive the subject. All four tests in this describe block read bin/e0-regression.sh as text (indexOf of the literals "HIT WALL CLOCK LIMIT" / "HIT ATTEMPT LIMIT (runaway guard)", a substring scan for `break`) and do arithmetic on profile keys; none constructs the required scenario «wall-clock budget remains but attempt count is exhausted ⇒ entry must continue». The repo already has a harness that really executes the entry with injected fake drains (setupE0RegressionEnv, test/e0c2-termination.test.ts:196-300), and the only entry-executing GT-19 test (test/e0c2-termination.test.ts:1050-1074) sets wallClockSeconds=1, i.e. the wall clock is exhausted immediately, and asserts only attempts>=1 — which held under the old count-first behavior too. The behavior fix landed (bin/e0-regression.sh:404-414 no longer breaks), but spec §5 requires 判据 2–4 tests to really drive the subject; this is the same blocker raised by the prior final review and it is unaddressed.

§1.1 forbids picking node_timeout by feel and requires measured p95/max single-tick durations from the timings instrumentation as the basis. The stated basis — «timings 埋点实测 p95 单 tick 耗时约 180s…最大 390s（dr-triage 观测值）» — has no provenance anywhere in the delivery: the TickTimings instrumentation is introduced by this same package (src/tick-run.ts:543-558), so it cannot have produced prior measurements, no captured tick output or run record carrying those numbers is committed, and the numbers appear in no ground truth (GT-18 records 30.5–39.9s engine kills and 221.084s/36.109s worker durations). The delivery's own dev-note reproduces the claim with an unfilled evidence block (`Test Files <n> passed (<n>)`), confirming nothing was recorded. An unverifiable measurement is exactly what §1.1 and §5 forbid.

判据 2b's duration assertion cannot discriminate. The test drives runChannelWrite with `fetch` stubbed and node:child_process.spawn module-mocked, so the elapsed time is a few in-process milliseconds and `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(nodeTimeout*1000*0.5)` passes identically at node_timeout=600 and at 30 — i.e. reverting the §1.1 fix does not turn this assertion red (only the adjacent literal check `nodeTimeout > 30`, a duplicate of 判据 2, would). GT-16's question is where the >30s goes on the --run side-effect path (bus I/O, spawn, waiting for worker results); every one of those stages is mocked out here, so the test measures nothing the criterion asks about.

The timings instrumentation offered as §1.1/§1.1b evidence does not measure the whole tick and does not break down the stage in question. `totalMs` is computed as tTerm - t0, but the generate段 (runGenerate, one of the slowest side-effect paths, and the exact step that produced GT-17's failure) runs after tTerm at lines 1736-1759 and is therefore excluded from every reported number. `writeSideMs` lumps CAS + spawn + harvest + triage into a single bucket, while §1.1b requires the 30 seconds to be split per stage (bus read/write, CAS, spawn, waiting for worker results, harvest, triage, continuation put) so the cost can be pinpointed.

DRAIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS no longer bounds anything. §1.1b allows keeping it as a runaway backstop that simply cannot fire before the wall clock; the delivered block only echoes a warning and re-runs read-termination/_print_board_composition on every subsequent iteration, with no break and no exit-code effect, so the count is now a pure log line. The profile comment (profiles/deploy/e0-regression.env:47-51) and the script comment still describe it as 失控兜底 with a self-consistency formula, which is now false — the wall clock is the only terminator, and after the limit is passed each round pays an extra termination read plus repeated stderr spam.

判据 2z asks that the tick still exit 0 through the entry with the diagnosis in its output. The test calls runChannelWrite directly and asserts diagnostics/decisions/triageReports on the returned object; it never exercises tick-entry --run, so neither the process exit code nor the presence of the diagnostic in stdout (which is what makes it grep-able per §1.1c) is asserted. The reverse case (bus unreachable ⇒ rejects) is covered.

The dev-note's evidence sections are unfilled or stale: the «全量测试尾部» block still contains the literal placeholders `Test Files <n> passed (<n>)` / `Tests <n> passed (<n>)` instead of a real run tail for 判据 1's two green runs, and the header cites input_commit d98d3a63fb4fd059aca237f70257bb815f71112b, which is not this attempt's base.

Confirmed as correctly delivered this round (non-blocking, recorded so it is not lost): the MAX_CLUES production assembly chain is now complete and end-to-end (bin/deep-research-loop.sh:126-128 export → fleet.yaml.tpl:26-28 → tick/workflow.yaml:46-48 → templates/tick.md:30,59-60 → tick-run.ts --max-clues at 1985-1992), which closes the continuous-review blocker from attempt 2; limits.wall_clock was raised 60 → 600 so it no longer truncates node_timeout; and the triage exited-without-result handler no longer reports the false `budgetSkipped: true` (src/tick-run.ts:885-900), with the generate path given the same record-and-continue treatment (src/tick-run.ts:1749-1756).
